title: Golomb-Dickman constant: 75,000 certified decimal digits
description:
Rigorous interval-arithmetic certificate for the first 75,000 decimal digits of the Golomb–Dickman constant

λ = ∫0∞ exp(−u − E1(u)) du = 0.624329988543550870992936383100837244…

The certificate consists of integers Λ− < Λ+ and a scale S = 249341 such that λ ∈ [Λ−/2S, Λ+/2S] and floor(1075000Λ−/2S) = floor(1075000Λ+/2S). The first 75,000 digits are therefore proved by truncation, not merely computed in floating point. The interval width is 5.8205594787 × 10−75043, leaving about 42.235 guard digits.

The computation uses the trapezoidal rule after the Takahashi–Mori substitution, explicit tail and discretisation bounds (Trefethen–Weideman), Stieltjes continued fractions for E1, and Arb balls via python-flint v0.9.0 on Linux x86_64 (Python 3.14.8). The package contains the certificate, a 75,000-digit file, the producing code, the 4,767 checkpoint chunks and checkers that use only the Python standard library and exact integer arithmetic. The first 50,000 and 40,000 digits agree with the earlier certificates.

Verification status: exact integer certificate check, digit file, OEIS prefix, plan parameters, chunk continuity and sums, and an independent mpmath quadrature at 320 digits all pass. A full Arb re-audit of all 476,648 nodes was not run (2,000 nodes were checked). This is an extension of a published computation, not a world-record claim; normality of the constant remains open.

Related: OEIS A084945 (decimal expansion), OEIS A225242 (Earls's sequence), MathWorld Golomb-Dickman Constant Digits, which cites the 40,000-digit result and a GitHub commit of this project.
